# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🤟 ✌ ✌ 🤟 ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤝]

I can see the bomb clearly: the display reads 0, the light is yellow, the large button says “PUSH TO DEFUSE,” and the wires are blue, yellow, red from positions 1 to 3. I’m sending all visible details to Mute so they can relay the necessary instructions to Blind.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb visible details: DISPLAY 0. LIGHT yellow. BUTTON large, labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE. WIRES in order: 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 red. Relay these exact details and the manual instructions to Blind.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 🖐 👌 🤚 ✌ ✋ 👊 🤞 ☝ ✌ 🤟 ☝ 🤟 ✌ 🫰 ☝ 🤟 ✌ ✌ 🤟 ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🫵 🫱 🫲]

The bomb’s visible state is unchanged. I cannot interpret the long gesture sequence as a reliable code because no gesture code has been established. I should therefore use speech to ensure Mute relays the bomb’s exact state and the manual’s procedure to Blind, who can then report tactile findings aloud.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot decode the gesture sequence without an agreed code. Please relay the bomb details I gave last turn, read the manual's exact instructions to Blind, and have Blind report any tactile findings and required action aloud.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👎 ☝ 🤞]

The bomb remains unchanged. The gestures still have no established meaning, so I cannot safely decode them. I am reinforcing the exact visual state to both teammates and asking Mute to transmit the manual’s procedure to Blind; Blind must not guess or act without that information.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Gestures are still undecodable. Please use speech to relay the exact bomb state and the manual's applicable procedure to Blind: display 0, yellow light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires blue-yellow-red.")
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb state is display 0, yellow light, large button labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires blue-yellow-red. Wait for Mute to read the manual procedure; do not guess.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝ 👍 ✌ 👍 🤟 👎 ☝ ✌ 🤟 👍 ☝ 👎]

The bomb still shows the same state, and I still have no agreed interpretation for Mute’s gestures. The safe path remains for Mute to read the relevant manual rule and communicate it by speech to Blind; I will restate the visual facts without asking Blind to guess.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please do not use gestures for the manual result. Speak the exact applicable instruction to Blind, including whether to press the large yellow-button case or cut a particular wire. Current visible state remains display 0, yellow light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 red.")
speak(to="blind", text="The visible state remains display 0, yellow light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 red. Do not act on my description alone; follow Mute's spoken manual instruction.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👍 ☝]

The bomb’s visible state is still unchanged. Mute’s gestures have no agreed meaning, so I cannot safely infer the manual’s rule from them. Mute can communicate the manual directly to Blind by speech, which is the reliable route to the hands; Blind should wait for that exact instruction.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the manual's exact applicable rule directly to Blind now. State the required action precisely: whether to press, hold, or release the large button, or which wire number and colour to cut. Do not rely on gestures.")
speak(to="blind", text="The bomb remains display 0, yellow light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 red. Wait for Mute's spoken manual rule and follow it exactly; do not guess.")
```

DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ☝]

The bomb remains unchanged. Mute’s latest gestures still have no established meaning, but we can fix that now. I’m defining a compact action code and asking Mute to resend the manual’s exact instruction using it; then I can speak the decoded instruction to Blind.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Use this gesture code for the manual answer: 👎 means CUT, 👍 means PRESS, 👌 means HOLD, ✋ means RELEASE, 🫵 means BUTTON, ☝ means WIRE 1, ✌ means WIRE 2, 🤟 means WIRE 3. Send the exact required action as a gesture sequence, and nothing else.")
speak(to="blind", text="The bomb remains display 0, yellow light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 red. I have just established a gesture code with Mute; wait for me to relay the decoded manual instruction before acting.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ☝]

Mute’s gesture sequence matches the code we established: 👎 means cut and ☝ means wire 1. Therefore the manual’s instruction is to cut wire 1, which is blue. I’m sending that exact action to Blind.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Decoded manual instruction: CUT WIRE 1. Wire 1 is blue. Cut the blue wire in position 1.")
```
